sections.h2: PVA, clerk and sheriff in Marshall County
sections.html:
Valuation and recording share one address, 1101 Main Street in Benton, where the PVA and the County Clerk keep offices. Collection of the bill belongs to the sheriff.

  • PVA: appraises property and takes exemption filings. The county directory shows 270-527-4767 as an alternate phone, with the office open on weekdays until 4:30.
  • Clerk: holds every land record in the county and collects delinquent property taxes. Call 270-527-4740.
  • Sheriff: collects county tax. A bill lookup and payment link sits on the sheriff's page at marshallcountyky.gov.

Tax collection is one job among several for the sheriff, whose deputies patrol about 300 square miles and more than 900 miles of road, work the lake with marine patrols, and provide court security.

A house inside Benton brings a second bill. City Hall, 1009 Main Street (270-527-8677), collects Benton's own property tax, and the city's website cautions residents against using its link for county taxes.

sections.h2: Kentucky Lake and Marshall County real estate
sections.html:
Water explains most of Marshall County's modern history. The Tennessee River and Kentucky Lake form its northeastern border, and 39 of its 340 square miles are water. In the 1940s the Tennessee Valley Authority impounded Kentucky Lake. Fishing resorts followed, and low-cost power from Kentucky Dam brought chemical and manufacturing plants to Calvert City. The impoundment flooded Birmingham and Gilbertsville, and Gilbertsville was rebuilt west of its first site.

Benton, the seat, is the biggest of the county's three cities, with Calvert City and Hardin the others. Gilbertsville is a census-designated place, and Aurora, Draffenville, Fairdealing and Briensburg are unincorporated. Owners of lakeside or second-home parcels should ask the PVA for the property's classification and last inspection date.

Marshall County leans older: one resident in four is 65 or over. Owners live in 81.6 percent of homes. The 2020 census counted 31,659 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is the same figure.

Housing units outnumber households by roughly 3,800, a gap that includes homes with no year-round household. Ask a local agent how many nearby listings are vacant or seasonal before you set a price.

Rates had to be finalized before the bills could be printed, so the Sheriff's Office set a collection start of November 1. The schedule it published:

  • November 1 to 30, 2026: two percent discount.
  • December 1 to 31, 2026: face amount due.
  • January 1 to 31, 2027: five percent penalty.
  • February 1 to April 15, 2027: ten percent penalty.

Such a shifted calendar is permitted by KRS 134.015(3), under which the Department of Revenue can swap in new dates when billing falls behind. In a normal year the two percent discount ends November 1, and the face amount is good through December.

Whatever the year, trust the dates printed on your own bill. When the cycle ends, open bills pass to the County Clerk, and the Department of Revenue says they then accrue one percent interest monthly.

sections.h2: Disputing a value that looks too high
sections.html:
Walk into the PVA's office and ask for a conference, the opening move in KRS 133.120. Still unconvinced? Put your reasons and your own fair-cash-value figure in a petition to the County Clerk no later than one workday after inspection ends, then prepare for the board hearing described in KRS 133.030.

  1. Gather neighborhood sales, an appraisal or construction costs.
  2. Attend yourself, or send someone with written authority.
  3. Keep paying on your own figure until the board decides.

An owner who bypasses the county board loses the later state appeal, so the petition deadline carries weight. Working farmland may qualify for agricultural-use valuation under Section 172A of the state constitution; ask the PVA about it.

Many owners qualify. About one resident in four is 65 or older, so the exemption touches a large share of homes. The $49,100 deduction for 2025 and 2026 comes off the assessed value. File with the Marshall County PVA, attaching proof of age or a disability classification. The benefit follows the owner, so a qualifying buyer files again.

sections.h2: Prices and buyers around the lake
sections.html:
Marshall County sellers fall into two groups: families selling a primary home, and owners letting go of lake or second-home property. The first group sells to local buyers, often from Benton and Calvert City, where the plants bring steady work. The second group draws buyers who want water access, so condition and the shoreline setting count for as much as square footage.

Because the median home value is $173,800 and building permits were only 86 in 2025, there is not a flood of new houses to compete with. Still, a seasonal property may have a different classification at the PVA than a full-time residence, and a buyer's lender will ask about it. Ask the PVA for the classification and the date of the last inspection before you list, and fix any mismatch in the owner name or mailing address on the roll so the next bill reaches the right person.

Working farmland may sell on its own terms. Section 172A of the state constitution allows agricultural-use valuation, so the tax figure a buyer sees may be lower than the price per acre would suggest. Share the actual bill with serious buyers rather than guessing.

A delinquency lien may remain for eleven years under KRS 134.015(5), so any unpaid year has to be cleared by closing. Because the Marshall County Clerk handles delinquent property tax, prior-year payoffs come from that office (270-527-4740) and the current bill from the sheriff.

Deeds are recorded with the same clerk, who first collects the grantor's transfer tax of fifty cents per $500 of value under KRS 142.050. The clerk lists open hours of 8 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays, with 270-527-4741 as a second line and 270-527-4746 for the vault. The homepage also promotes protection against deed theft, which any seller should ask about after closing.

Plan the order of your errands. Get the current payoff from the sheriff and any earlier-year payoff from the clerk, hand both letters to the closing agent, and bring the signed deed to the clerk with the transfer tax. If the city of Benton bills your house too, ask City Hall for that balance as well, because it is a separate account. A cash sale skips the lender's schedule, so these payoffs are usually the last items between you and the closing date.

faqs.q: Where can I look up my Marshall County tax bill?
faqs.a: Use the bill lookup and payment link on the Sheriff's page of the county website. For value or exemption questions, ask the PVA at 1101 Main Street in Benton.

faqs.q: Do Benton residents pay a separate city property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Benton collects it separately, at City Hall, 1009 Main Street (270-527-8677). Do not use the city's link for Marshall County taxes.

faqs.q: What was the Marshall County discount for 2026 bills?
faqs.a: Two percent on payments from November 1 through November 30, 2026. Face amount applied through December 2026.

faqs.q: Which Marshall County office collects delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: The County Clerk, at 1101 Main Street in Benton. Interest of one percent a month starts once bills reach the clerk.

faqs.q: What is the Marshall County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: It takes $49,100 off assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, for owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled and who apply at the PVA.
